analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog.d entry and an edit to docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (head lines 393-400). No executable source is supplied, so the implementation (SSDWriteBehind.chargeWholeDonation) was not examined. The docs describe a behavior change in the SSD prefix-cache write-budget ledger. An attention donation now reserves the summed size of its blocks in one charge before the first write. If that charge is refused (near the cap or while another writer holds the ledger), the code falls back to a per-block charge, so the leading blocks that fit are still written. Blocks skipped after the donation charge stay charged, with no refunds.

As documented, the invariants in T-041 (SSD write-endurance and at-rest posture, with the write cap among its guards) are preserved:
- Charges precede writes.
- Charges are never refunded.
- The ledger fails closed on corrupt or inaccessible accounting.
- The ledger records only time buckets and byte counts.

No new data exposure is described, and no change to the DBK3 format, HMAC names, TTL, KEK handling or identity binding.

Open questions for any pass that sees the code: whether the donation-level charge is always applied before the first write, including on the fallback path; whether charge accounting stays correct when blocks are skipped mid-donation (over-charge is conservative); whether a failed or partial reservation can ever permit uncharged writes; and whether summing sizes can overflow or understate the serialized DBK3 size, which would weaken the daily cap. These cannot be verified from docs alone. The claim that a refused ledger charge no longer blocks other models as often is an availability improvement, not a security regression. I report no findings.
